Heating up the grill…
Food Safety Learning

Would you eat from this grill?

A busy cafeteria has five skewers turning. Spot the food safety problems and fix them before service.

Grill fixed

✕ Still wrong

Raw chicken goes on the bottom rows

Raw poultry juice can carry Salmonella and Campylobacter. Anything that drips must land on raw chicken or the tray, never on cooked chicken.

✕ Still wrong

Throw the gravy drippings away

The gravy pan under the grill fills with raw chicken juice all day. Serving it as gravy passes those bacteria on to customers.

✕ Still wrong

Throw away the leftover half chicken

It sat in the drip tray under raw chicken, so it is contaminated. Keep leftover portions in hot holding, outside the grill machine.

One more thing: the cooked chicken that sat under the raw rows has already been dripped on. In a real kitchen it should be thrown away or fully re-cooked. Switch on germ vision to see it.
